add: trueup.py trues up an account only when its September the 1st read has read code A; an account whose closing read is an estimate gets no true up and its August month is billed as read.
prompt_tail: Billing wants this as trueup.py, a script they can point at next month's export and rate schedule without editing it: reads.csv first, tariff.csv second. It should print the statement batch and send one tally line to stderr as accounts=N august=N trueup=N corrected=N due=N, where due is every account's amount due added up. The batch starts with the statement month and four figures, the number of accounts, the August charges added together in cents, the true up amounts added together in cents and how many accounts carry a true up, then gives each account a block in the order it first turns up in the export: its August usage and charge, then for an account that trued up a line for each corrected month with the corrected usage and charge beside what was billed, and the true up amount, and last the amount due. Month names on the statement should come from the read dates rather than being typed in. Save September's run as statement_2026_09.txt with a few lines of your own above it on what moved this month. In README.md, say how to run it, take one trued-up account from its two actual readings to its amount due by hand so billing can see the script lands on the same units and cents, and note where a true up goes wrong. Don't change reads.csv or tariff.csv, and the readings stay on this machine.
